goal: Build the floor. These three carry the vocabulary every later lesson assumes, and they are the ones that take longest to sink in, so they go first while there is still room.
drill: The exam questions are inside each lesson now. Answer all 25 in the Big Picture and all 16 in Number Systems before you stop.

window: Tuesday evening, 6:30 pm to 9:00 pm, straight after the INS224 paper
goal: Every calculation topic in one run. Signed numbers, IEEE 754, sizing, formats, addressing, performance and pipelining are all formula work with a worked example you can copy under pressure, so they read fast.
drill: The 46 exam questions sitting inside those lessons. Anything you miss, reread that block before moving on.

goal: Sit the 2024/25 paper against the clock. Two hours, closed book, then read only the parts you could not finish. It is the friendlier of the two papers, which is why it comes first.
drill: Nothing new tonight. Sleep matters more than one more topic.

goal: Memory and cache with a fresh head. It is 26 of the 120 exam questions, more than any other block, and the mapping arithmetic punishes tiredness. Then RISC and CISC, then the one-page summary read slowly.
drill: All 26 memory and cache questions inside that lesson, then anything the mastery map still shows untested.

window: Wednesday, 7:00 am to 9:00 am, then leave for the hall
goal: Sit the 2025/26 paper, the most recent one, against the clock. Two hours, no notes, then read only the answers you got wrong.
drill: Nothing new. Re-read the night-before page in the last fifteen minutes.
